A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OpticalDNA work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original eQTL prediction, rice classification, whole-genome phenotype prediction, OCR evaluations and ablation results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds controlled comparisons, rendering robustness, token bottleneck, computational cost, contamination and cross-species transfer analyses.

M1.justification: The DNA rendering pipeline, visual encoder, projector, fusion module, document decoder, six pretraining tasks and training objective are retained. The new token-merging variants are experimental ablations; they do not replace the proposed OpticalDNA procedure.

E1.justification: The biological corpora, nine eQTL tissues, five rice groups and two phenotype tasks remain unchanged. Beyond v1's rendering-resolution sweep, v2 adds input scenarios involving alternate fonts, layouts, fragment boundaries and downsampling with DNA content and layout held fixed (Section 4.7 and Appendix N).

E2.justification: Table 2 adds NT-v2-500M and GENERator-1.2B. Appendix A adds BiGRU/RNN, Performer/LinearAttn, Longformer/SparseAttn and two Transformer baselines. Appendix O additionally compares Caduceus and JanusDNA on RiceSubBench and adds Caduceus to RiceWGPB. These substantially broaden the evaluated comparator sets.

E3.justification: v2 adds chunked, frozen-backbone linear-probe evaluation for NT and GENERator; a shared-Transformer comparison with 10,000 tokens per representation; and a unified computational-cost protocol. It also introduces length-stratified OCR, token-pooling, contamination and representation-consistency evaluations, and tests HG38-pretrained models on rice. The original pretraining schedules and benchmark splits remain as stated.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether the advantage survives stronger sequence architectures, matched backbone/token budgets and a common pretraining source. Further additions examine contamination, OCR failure by retained length, token bottlenecks, rendering perturbations and representation consistency (Appendices A, I, K.1 and L–O). The original OCR, masked-span and Grad-CAM analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain seeded hashing for RiceSubBench and seed=42 for RiceWGPB. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, performance confidence intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Original benchmark scores remain unchanged, including OpticalDNA's 0.852/0.867 average eQTL AUROC. New results include NT/GENERator averages of 0.772/0.782, matched-budget 1D/2D AUROC of 0.558/0.626, token-bottleneck results ranging from 0.852 at 100 tokens to 0.776 at one token, and HG38-to-rice transfer results. v2 also adds extensive robustness, contamination and computational-cost measurements; these are additional results under their stated conditions.

T1.justification: The document and coordinate definitions, generative objective, curriculum formula, ROI metrics and Grad-CAM equations are retained. The added motivation and empirical analyses introduce no substantive new mathematical derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: OCR-style genomic modeling, six prompted tasks, improved prediction and efficient visual compression. The headline nearly 20-fold token reduction and 985-fold activated-parameter comparison remain unchanged. Additional supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendix B explicitly explains the visual layout as a computational interface without biologically grounded 2D geometry or annotation priors. Other additions argue against memorization and rice-specific pretraining as explanations, and identify limits involving long OCR spans, severe token bottlenecks and disrupted sequence continuity. These substantially expand the mechanism discussion and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 adds front-page project and code links, a detailed rendering-configuration grid, and implementation descriptions such as adjacent-token pooling with tail handling. Table 2 relabels parameter counts as trainable, and Table S36 separately reports total inference parameters. Existing pretraining hyperparameters, hardware descriptions and baseline reproduction instructions are largely retained; linked repository contents cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds the GENERator citation to Wu et al. (2025) and replaces the Consortium (2019) genome-reference citation with Schneider et al. (2017). The related-work sections and claimed novelty of the OCR-style genomic formulation remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and technical exposition are retained. v2 adds a motivation appendix, subdivides Appendix A, retitles Section 4.6, inserts robustness and transfer sections, condenses the impact statement and updates acknowledgements and front matter. These are limited editorial and organizational changes alongside the scientific additions.

P2.justification: v2 adds rendering, downsampling and transfer plots, a multi-panel representation-consistency heatmap, and numerous tables presenting new controls and analyses. Table 2 gains comparison columns, while Figure 3 corrects its legend from VisualDNA to OpticalDNA without changing its results. Existing displays are also repositioned. The new Figure 7 has an incorrect caption describing resolution-dependent eQTL results despite plotting rice transfer.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens assessment of the central representation claim through shared-backbone/token-budget controls, stronger baselines and pretraining-source controls that v1 lacked. Rendering, bottleneck and computational-cost analyses also expose practical strengths and failure regimes. These gains outweigh the added reporting problems, but the contamination assurance remains limited: Table S25 uses 11,253 and 16,569 RiceWGPB test sequences, whereas retained Table S23 lists only 21 and 26 test accessions, without reconciling the counts or units. Repeated-run uncertainty is still absent.
